items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: he arranged things that would allow Buddy Banks to stay in Switzerland as long as I stayed and only if he worked with me.

ctx.x: Mr. Tripet had been a colonel in the Swiss army and he could pull some strings with the government when it was necessary to do so, and he arranged things that would allow Buddy Banks to stay in Switzerland as long as I stayed and only if he worked with me. Then suddenly, Banks and Randy Downs got the idea that they wanted to go back to Paris and one week before my contract finished at the Chikito, they told me they were leaving.

Banks had a great influence on Randy who was a fine pianist, but young and easily influenced by a person like Banks,who was also a fine bassist, but wild and irresponsible. We closed on the 15th of January, 1953, and they left for Paris the next day I suppose.

Lily and I also came to Paris to engage replacements for Banks and Randy. I had five concerts booked in Switzerland after finishing at the Chikito and was booked for the month of February in St.Gallen which was near the German border.
